Fourth, we replace client layout simulation with server-computed 3D Cone-Tree/Ribbon coordinates and a non-WebGL 2.5D Isometric projection with painter's-order depth sorting and sub-millisecond Level-of-Detail (LoD) macro-cuts.

items.title: Approximation Algorithms for Maximum-Weight Degree-Bounded Forests
items.summary: In the maximum-weight degree-bounded forest problem, we are given a graph with nonnegative edge weights and a degree upper bound on each vertex. The objective is to find a maximum-weight forest satisfying the degree bounds. We show that this problem admits a simple $2$-approximation via the greedy algorithm. This already improves over the best-known guarantees obtained via a reduction to weighted $3$-matroid parity, and sets a baseline to improve upon. Our main result is an $\frac{8}{5}$-approximation algorithm for the maximum-weight degree-bounded forest problem. For the special case of uniform degree bounds, our algorithm achieves an approximation ratio of $\frac{3}{2}$. It computes two sets of edges, each of which we then restrict to a feasible solution in an optimal way, and finally returns the better of the two resulting solutions. To obtain the initial two edge sets, we first relax the degree bounds and leverage an algorithm by Lau and Singh [JACM'15] for degree-bounded spanning trees, and second we relax the forest constraints and employ an algorithm for maximum-weight $b$-matchings.

items.title: Efficient Lempel-Ziv Prediction with the Run-Length BWT
items.summary: Lempel-Ziv Plurality (LZP) is an algorithm of Kosoy that predicts the next symbol of a string by using its Lempel-Ziv factorization, and makes at most $O(z\log n)$ mistakes on every string of length $n$ with $z$ LZ77 phrases. We give efficient online implementations of LZP and of a new variant of it. Our first implementation maintains a run-length encoded Burrows-Wheeler transform (RLBWT) of the reversed history. It implements LZP, uses $O(z\log z\log^2 n)$ bits, and has worst-case update and prediction times $O(\log z+\log\log n)$ and $O(σ(\log z+\log\log n))$, respectively, where $σ$ is the size of the alphabet. This is an exponential improvement over Kosoy's implementation, whose update time is $O(z\log^7 n)$. We then introduce the Lempel-Ziv Majority (LZM) predictor, which has the same mistake bound and update time, and predicts in $O(1)$ time independently of $σ$. These two predictors accept new symbols at any time, without knowing the alphabet in advance. For an alphabet known in advance, a different data structure gives $O(σ(1+\log z/\log\log n))$ time per symbol, which is constant when $σ=O(1)$ and $z=\mathrm{polylog}(n)$.

items.title: Recent Developments in HPR Methods for Large-Scale Linear Programming
items.summary: We present recent developments in Halpern Peaceman-Rachford (HPR) methods for solving large-scale linear programming problems. We first introduce the semi-proximal HPR framework and summarize its convergence guarantees, together with its connections to Halpern PDHG and ergodic Peaceman-Rachford iterations. To improve practical performance, we develop adaptive restart and penalty parameter update strategies. We then describe several computational enhancements, including GPU-based preprocessing, diagonal scaling, reusable execution plans for sparse matrix-vector multiplication, and sieving techniques. We further discuss multi-GPU parallelization and lossless model storage and loading for handling large-scale instances. These developments form the foundation of HPR-LP, a GPU-accelerated solver for large-scale linear programming.

items.title: On Exact Dual and Mixed-Integer Reformulations for Finite Horizon Markov Decision Processes with Submodular Revenue Maximization
items.summary: We study exact mixed-integer reformulations of a finite horizon Markov decision process (MDP) with transition revenues defined by local submodular revenue maximization problems. We start with the dual linear programming formulation of the MDP, where local optimal revenues appear in the objective function and the constraints describe the state probabilities from the initial state. We combine the dual formulation with the binary variables of the local problems and obtain an exact mixed-integer nonlinear formulation with bilinear terms. We use the submodular inequalities and an exact McCormick linearization to obtain an equivalent mixed-integer linear formulation. We also use the dual structure to conduct a sensitivity analysis of the MDP optimal value with respect to changes in the local revenue coefficients. Based on local incumbent revenues and upper bounds, this sensitivity analysis evaluates the effect of local optimality gaps on the global MDP optimality gap, without solving every local revenue maximization problem to optimality.

items.title: Integral saturation of adjacency-degree lattices
items.summary: Let $A$ be the adjacency matrix of $G\sim G(n,1/2)$, let $D=\operatorname{diag}(A\mathbf{1})$, and let $Λ_G=\mathbb{Z}\langle A,D\rangle\mathbf{1}$. We prove $\Pr[Λ_G\ne\mathbb{Z}^n]\le n^{-3/20+o(1)}$. Thus two dependent graph operators generate the entire vertex lattice from the constant vector, simultaneously over every prime field. Adjacency alone has a modulo-two rank obstruction for every simple graph of order greater than one, even though its rational word span is typically full. The proof first constructs words containing at most two adjacency operations whose integer span contains $Δ_G^3\mathbb{Z}^n$, where $Δ_G$ is the product of the pairwise differences between distinct degree values. This confines all possible arithmetic obstructions to a finite prime range on a single event. We then remove the remaining obstructions using conditional alternating forms, symmetric random-matrix code estimates, and uniform counts of degree-graded invariant subspaces. We connect the integer lattice to graph reconstruction through pointed moments. Saturation forces every pointed orthogonal AD intertwiner to be a vertex permutation. The short-word construction also shows that a fixed polynomial-size family of ordinary caterpillars, of diameter at most seven and order $O(\sqrt{n\log n})$, identifies almost every graph among all finite simple graphs. For nonsaturated full-rank lattices, we give an exact description of the moment fibre by admissible unimodular overlattices; at index two, the only possible ambiguity is a specified four-vertex Godsil--McKay switch.

items.title: Instance-Specific Sharp Convergence Rate of the Add-$λ$ Estimator via Feature Space Decomposition
items.summary: Using the Feature Space Decomposition framework, we establish non-asymptotic matching upper and lower bounds for the expected Kullback-Leibler estimation error of the Add-$λ$ estimator of a discrete probability distribution, for any signal, any dimension, any sample size, and any $λ>0$.

items.title: Multi-rate high-order regularization with an order-$(p-2)$ oracle
items.summary:
We consider unconstrained minimization of a possibly nonconvex function $f:\mathbb{R}^n	o\mathbb{R}$ whose $p$th derivative is Lipschitz continuous, with $p\geq3$, when derivative information is available only through order $p-2$. The unavailable tensors $
abla^{p-1}f$ and $
abla^pf$ are reconstructed from central finite differences of $
abla^{p-2}f$. Since the two reconstructions have different point-query costs, we use a block length $m$ for the order-$p$ approximation and a subblock length $\ell\leq m$ for the order-$(p-1)$ approximation. The latter is transported between consecutive reconstruction points using the stored order-$p$ approximation. This leads to an adaptive regularization method that does not require prior knowledge of the Lipschitz constant. We prove finite termination at an $ε$-approximate first-order stationary point and derive an explicit bound on the number of bundled order-$(p-2)$ oracle queries. For $m=(p-2)n^2$ and $\ell=(p-2)n$, the accuracy-dependent term has dimension--accuracy scaling $n^{3/p}ε^{-(p+1)/p}$. Thus the method retains the $ε^{-(p+1)/p}$ dependence of full order-$p$ regularization while using derivatives only through order $p-2$. Within the dense reconstruction framework considered here, using separate block and subblock lengths gives dimension dependence of order $n^{3/p}$, compared with $n^{4/p}$ when a common length is imposed.

items.title: Monotone Local Search with Sample-Dependent Running Times
items.summary: Monotone Local Search turns an algorithm that extends a given partial solution into an algorithm that finds a solution from scratch: sample a few elements, hope that they lie in an unknown solution, and complete them. Its known analyses bound every call of the extension algorithm by a worst-case time that depends only on the number of sampled elements, and Esmer et al. (SODA 2024) showed that no algorithm that uses the extension algorithm as a black box with this running time beats the original form by more than a polynomial factor. We let this running time depend on the actual sample. If the extension algorithm decides in time $O^*(2^{g(I,X,k)})$, for a polynomial-time computable $g$, whether a sample $X$ can be completed to a solution with at most $k$ elements, our main theorem gives a randomized algorithm with one-sided error in time $O^*(2^{ψn})$ whenever, for some solution $S$ of size $k$ and some $t$, the exponential moment $\sum_{X\subseteq S,|X|=t}2^{-g(I,X,k)}$ is at least $2^{-ψn}\binom{n}{t}$. A corollary, multivariate Monotone Local Search, generalizes the theorems of Fomin et al. (STOC 2016, J. ACM 2019) and of Gaspers and Lee (ICALP 2017). For Max Leaf Spanning Tree and, equivalently, Connected Dominating Set, the previous best polynomial-space bound is $O^*(1.8619^n)$. Completing a sample is a Steiner tree problem, solved in time exponential in the number of terminals, which varies strongly with the sample. We obtain a randomized polynomial-space algorithm in time $O(1.6991^n)$ and a deterministic one in time $(\sqrt5-\frac12)^n 2^{o(n)}=O(1.7361^n)$. For connectivity problems in which the extension algorithm's running time doubles with every component of the sample, an analysis through a partition function gives randomized polynomial-space algorithms in time $O^*(1.8^n)$ for Connected Feedback Vertex Set and $O(1.6444^n)$ for Connected Vertex Cover.

items.title: Optimization Frameworks & Learning Algorithms for Discrete-Time Mean Field Games
items.summary: This monograph introduces discrete-time mean field games with finite state and action spaces, emphasizing optimization formulations and learning algorithms. Starting from Markov decision processes and finite-player stochastic games, it develops the notion of mean field Nash equilibrium, establishes existence and uniqueness results under suitable assumptions, and explains how mean field equilibria yield approximate equilibria in large finite-player games. Building on the linear programming formulation of Markov decision processes, occupation measures and primal-dual formulations connect equilibrium computation with mathematical optimization. The monograph presents fixed-point iterations, fictitious play, online mirror descent, and optimization-based methods, discussing their convergence properties and limitations. Numerical examples illustrate crowd motion, traffic routing, epidemic management, and the computation of multiple equilibria. It combines examples, theoretical results, and implementable algorithms, with bibliographic notes providing connections to the broader literature.

items.title: On Sequential Entropic Optimal Transport Filter and its Multilevel Variants
items.summary: We consider the problem of filtering partially observed diffusions associated to discrete time observations. This problem requires the development of advanced numerical methods such as particle filters. In this article we develop a new sequential entropic optimal transport filter (EOTF). The main idea is to sample from successive couplings of the filters. To achieve this, we adopt the approach of an entropic optimal transport (EOT) update implemented through a learned Schrödinger potential, in the spirit of the light Schrödinger bridge methodology \cite{korotin2024light}. Based on this, we develop a multilevel version of this filter (ML-EOTF) in which consecutive discretization levels are coupled at the terminal time by a scaled EOT plan with level-dependent regularization $\eps_l=\eps_0 h_l^κ$ with discretization stepsize $h_l$. Under mild conditions, we show that the level-difference estimator with exact Schrödinger potentials has variance of order $N_l^{-1}\{h_l^β+\eps_l\}$, where $β$ is the strong-error for the discretized SDE. The analysis is then extended to learned potentials, with all approximation and optimization errors summarized by a joint Kullback--Leibler discrepancy whose contribution to the mean squared error is explicitly quantified. Combined with a fixed-time weak-error estimate, this yields the canonical multilevel complexity $\cO(δ^{-2}|\logδ|^2)$ to achieve an MSE of $δ^2$ for Euler--Maruyama discretizations. Numerical experiments validate the results.

items.title: The maximum concentration of results in incomplete round-robin tournaments
items.summary: The Herfindahl--Hirschman Index (HHI), a standard measure of market concentration, is widely used to quantify competitive balance in sports tournaments. To enable comparisons over time or across leagues, both its minimum and maximum should be known. The minimum is usually trivial. Our paper provides results on the maximum HHI in incomplete round-robin tournaments, where the set of matches is represented by a regular but not complete undirected graph. We prove that the lower bound of maximum HHI is reached when the tournament consists of independent round-robin groups, while the upper bound of maximum HHI is reached when the set of matches is represented by a bipartite graph. Maximising HHI is computationally difficult even for highly structured graph types corresponding to real-world tournaments, where the teams are partitioned into pots and play the same number of matches against opponents from every pot. The complexity of the problem does not depend on the scoring system or the number of opponents from a pot.

items.title: Convex Regression at Scale: Geometry-Preserving Constraint Sparsification
items.summary: Convex regression provides a flexible nonparametric estimation framework while incorporating appropriate shape information. However, its standard least-squares formulation has $O(n^2)$ supporting-hyperplane constraints creating a computational bottleneck as the sample size $n$ increases. We study a $K$-nearest-neighbor (KNN) localized relaxation for convex regression where we for each sample, we only maintain the $K$ nearest hyperplane constraints. Under mild regularity conditions, we establish statistical guarantees for our modified estimator in every fixed dimension $d\ge2$. In particular, for $d>4$, the population risk of our modified problem can be shown to have equivalent convergence rates as the original least square convex regression estimator of $\widetilde O(n^{-2/d})$ using neighborhoods sizes (i.e. $K=K_n$) of order $\widetilde O(n^{2(d-1)/(2d-1)})$ for general convex functions and $\widetilde O(n^{(d+1)/(d+2)})$ for strongly convex functions. To corroborate our theory, we implement iterative optimization methods to compare the prediction accuracy of the KNN relaxation with those of the full estimator across synthetic convex benchmarks. Our experiments demonstrate that KNN prediction risk approaches the full-estimator prediction risk at neighborhood sizes matching the theoretical scale.

items.title: Singular Tracking of Fractional Brownian Motion under Proportional Costs
items.summary: We study adapted finite-variation tracking of fractional Brownian motion under quadratic loss and proportional adjustment costs. For $H\in(0,1)$, \[ V_λ(T;a,b,σ)\underset{λ\downarrow0}{\sim}κ_HT a^{(1-H)/(1+H)}(λb)^{2H/(1+H)}σ^{2/(1+H)}. \] The positive long-run cell value $κ_H$ is unchanged by full past information. A bounded full-past reset correction yields finite-horizon bounds and continuity in $H$. The Brownian value is $κ_{1/2}=\frac12(\frac32)^{2/3}$. Coupling local paths with their filtrations gives a local limit, which we verify for Gaussian Volterra targets. Every asymptotically optimal control has the same leading tracking--variation cost split. Primal and dual bounds quantify the cell value. For $H<1/2$, we construct a positive-factor approximation and relate factor resolution to horizon length.

items.title: Assessing Temporal Dispersion of Time-Varying Channel at 38 GHz for Different Reference Signals
items.summary: This paper investigates the influence of reference waveform selection on temporal dispersion estimation in a time-varying radio channel at 38 GHz. Three reference waveforms-numerically generated in MATLAB, measured through a conducted connection, and recorded in an anechoic chamber -are compared using the same wideband channel measurements conducted in a dynamic road environment. Their effects on the estimated power delay profiles (PDPs), mean delay, and root mean square (RMS) delay spread are evaluated. Despite noticeable differences in the time-domain and spectral characteristics of the reference waveforms, the resulting PDPs exhibit similar multipath structures, while the estimated temporal dispersion parameters show relatively small differences. The results indicate limited sensitivity to reference waveform selection under the investigated measurement conditions.

items.title: Communication with Adversarial Users: Byzantine Models in Multi-User Information Theory
items.summary: We consider communication systems operating in environments where some participating users cannot be trusted. This motivates the study of Byzantine communication models, in which users may behave adversarially. In this survey, we provide a unified information-theoretic perspective on communication with adversarial users in multi-user settings. We review recent advances in Byzantine multiple access channels, including reliable communication, adversary identification, and distributed function computation. Furthermore, we discuss extensions to classical-quantum channels and highlight fundamental differences between classical and quantum models. Finally, we outline key open problems and future research directions at the intersection of communication, computation, and security.

items.title: How Much Does Random Rotation Help GPTQ? Sharp Worst-Case Rate Gaps in the High-Rate Regime
items.summary: GPTQ is Babai's nearest-plane algorithm on the lattice of the Cholesky factor of the layer's input second moment $Σ$. In the high-rate, entropy-coded regime it needs $\tfrac12\log_2(\AM/\GM)$ of its Cholesky pivots more bits than WaterSIC, which is within $0.255$ bit of the rate-distortion limit for every $Σ$; random rotations close most of this gap in practice, and Ordentlich and Polyanskiy asked for the worst-case gap between rotated GPTQ and WaterSIC. We show that after a Haar rotation the $k$-th pivot converges almost surely, uniformly in $k\geδn$ and over spectra $ν$ of bounded condition number, to $1/S_ν(-k/n)$, a classical formula from the theory of Lyapunov exponents, and use it to answer the question. Over spectra with condition number $κ$ the worst rotated gap is $\tfrac12\log_2κ-\log_2\lnκ+\tfrac12-\tfrac1{\ln2}+o(1)$ bits, attained only by two-point spectra, just $\tfrac12\log_2\lnκ+O(1)$ bits below the worst case without rotation, so rotation cannot replace waterfilling in general. It nearly can on real layers: rotation cuts the cost of an $η$-fraction of outlier eigenvalues of size $μ$ from about $ημ$ to $η^2μ/2$ to leading order, but cannot remove spectral spread on a logarithmic scale; for non-Gaussian weights it also adds a weight-side rate cost, which we characterize exactly under a standard high-rate assumption. On $96$ Hessians of Qwen3 and Llama-3.1 the rotated gap has median $0.04$ bit and maximum $0.36$ bit, against $2$--$5$ bits in the worst case for the same condition numbers, and the limit matches it to within $0.009$ bit.

items.title: Multirate Data-Driven Predictive Control: Rank Obstructions, Identifiability, and Noise Conditioning
items.summary: We develop rank, identifiability, and noise-conditioning results for compact input--output predictors in multirate data-driven predictive control. The inverse of a square zero-input response matrix used in an existing compact-lifting construction is shown to be undefined under its observability and minimal-polynomial assumptions. We derive exact replacements using rank-complete data, characterize all predictor extensions, and establish the minimum-norm and minimax Euclidean noise properties of the canonical Moore--Penrose extension. A joint predictor is identified directly from mixed experiments with arbitrary initial states. Deterministic perturbation bounds quantify reconstruction errors through informative singular-value margins, while a positive-definite reduced weighting preserves the nominal quadratic cost. Sampling-rate observability and event-triggering analyses identify additional conditions needed for reconstruction and stability guarantees.

items.title: Long-Time Behavior of Zero-Noise Mean-Field Adam
items.summary: Adaptive methods such as Adam are the most commonly used methods for training neural networks, but their long-time behavior is not as well understood as that of non-adaptive methods. This is particularly true in the mean-field limit, where the dynamics of infinitely many neurons are described as a distribution over parameters which satisfies a self-consistency condition. In this paper, we study a deterministic continuous-time model of Adam in the mean-field setting. Under a condition relating the averaging rates of the momentum and second-moment variables, the size of the gradients, and a regularization parameter, we prove that the distribution of parameters converges to the set of equilibria. This condition extends the range known for finite-dimensional models, and we show that it is sharp. Under an additional Lojasiewicz-type inequality for distributions, we prove that individual parameter trajectories converge and obtain quantitative rates for this convergence. We verify the qualitative convergence assumptions for a regularized two-layer neural network. We also show that adding noise to the momentum prevents the system from approaching these equilibria and rules out many free-energy type Lyapunov functionals. Finally, numerical experiments illustrate the energy estimates, give evidence of persistent oscillations outside the sufficient parameter range, and compare the observed decay with the predicted rates.

items.title: Worst-User Outage Probability Minimization in Active RIS-Aided Systems
items.summary: In this paper, a worst-user outage probability minimization problem in active reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-aided systems is addressed. Since the resulting problem involves a discontinuous objective function over an unknown channel distribution, a sequence of reformulations is applied by integrating a probability-simplex user weighting, a softplus surrogate for differentiability, and entropic tail-risk aggregation for rare but severe outage events. Based on the reformulated problem, a data-driven stochastic optimization technique that relies on historical channel samples is adopted to jointly optimize the beamformer and reflection coefficients with projected adaptive moment estimation. Simulation results show advantages of the proposed technique for reliability-oriented active RIS transmission design.

items.title: OCP-Based Nonlinear Model Predictive Control for Quadrotor Trajectory Tracking
items.summary: Fast online optimization is essential for nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) on resource-limited aerial platforms. This paper presents an analytical-derivative NMPC solver for quadrotor trajectory tracking. For the state-affine translational model with held thrust and attitude commands, fourth-order Runge--Kutta integration yields an exact discrete-time prediction map. Forward--backward difference equations provide the gradient and exact Hessian of the finite-horizon cost condensed over the input sequence. These derivatives drive a nested optimal-control-based direction recursion, while a shifted warm start reuses the preceding solution. The resulting solver addresses the unconstrained tracking problem without a general-purpose nonlinear programming package. Gazebo experiments show comparable tracking accuracy to iLQR and two acados SQP configurations, with mean solver-time speedups of $1.97$--$2.30$. In onboard flight tests, the mean solver time is $0.3121$\,ms, corresponding to speedups of $3.37$--$5.77$ over the same baselines. The largest measured solver time is $3.7754$\,ms within a $20$-ms control period. These measurements cover the numerical solver and exclude estimation, communication, and command publication.

items.title: Mean Field Game Problem with Kantorovich Potential Coupling: An Attrition model
items.summary: In this work we address a class of Mean-Field Game (MFG) systems on the flat torus $\mathbb{T}^{d}$ in which individual agent incentives arise from macroscopic, distribution-dependent objectives governed by the Wasserstein-2 ($W_{2}$) distance. Taking the first variation (Lions derivative) of the Wasserstein-based macroscopic functional yields a coupled forward-backward system of Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman (HJB) and Fokker--Planck (FP) equations featuring a nonlocal coupling driven by the Kantorovich optimal transport potential. As a primary case study, we formulate a large-scale attacker-defender attrition model aimed at protecting High-Value Units (HVUs). By defining population-wise attrition rates via the $W_{2}$ metric and casting the defense strategy as a Pareto-optimal McKean--Vlasov control problem, we derive a concrete HJB--FP system with a Kantorovich potential coupling. We prove the local-in-time existence of classical solutions for this system using Schauder's fixed-point theorem. Finally, we compute the MFG dynamics by combining the Sinkhorn algorithm with ResNet-based Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs), and simulate two-dimensional attacker-defender engagements across diverse attrition parameters, control costs, and multi-HVU configurations.

items.title: Fresh-Priority Eviction for Cuckoo Filters: Exploiting Latent Randomness Under XOR Hashing
items.summary: Cuckoo filters are a widely adopted approximate membership query (AMQ) data structure that supports insertions, lookups, and deletions with low memory overhead. At high load factors, however, insertion performance degrades sharply due to the random-walk eviction process, which may require a large number of element relocations. Recent work on bucketized cuckoo hash tables has shown that \emph{fresh-priority eviction}, which preferentially evicts elements whose alternate bucket location has not yet been used, achieves $O(\ell m)$ total expected evictions for bucket size~$\ell$, an improvement over the standard random walk. In this paper, we show that this technique transfers to \emph{cuckoo filters} despite their use of XOR-based partial-key hashing. The key insight is that a fresh element's fingerprint, although stored in the table, is not examined by the eviction policy, so when the fingerprint length satisfies $k = Ω(\log m)$, the alternate bucket hash remains a near-uniform random variable, a property we call \emph{latent randomness}. We prove that under this condition the corruption graph remains subcritical and the total number of evictions is $O(\ell m \log m)$; we conjecture the tighter $O(\ell m)$ bound holds via the full amortized analysis of Bell and Kuszmaul. We further propose encoding the fresh/kicked state implicitly by the element's position within its bucket, requiring no additional per-element metadata. Experimental results on a filter with $2^{22}$ slots and $8$-bit fingerprints demonstrate $1.2\times$ to $2.4\times$ fewer evictions at load factors between $94\%$ and $99\%$ for bucket size $\ell = 8$, and a $1.73\times$ reduction in cumulative evictions to full capacity.

items.title: Energy-Dissipative, High-Order BDF Schemes for Simulating Geometric Flows via Energy Increments
items.summary: We propose energy-dissipative backward differentiation formula (BDF) methods for geometric flows in the Barrett--Garcke--Nürnberg (BGN) parametric finite element framework. Starting from a Lagrange-multiplier formulation, we replace the multistep approximation of the energy derivative by an energy-increment equation while retaining the BDF geometric equations. The Simpson quadrature and two interleaved time grids provide third- and fourth-order constructions. The positive quadrature weights ensure stepwise decay of the original discrete geometric energy for every nondegenerate solution of the nonlinear system. We establish an explicit conditional consistency bound for the scalar energy equation and a regularity criterion for the Newton system of curve-shortening flows. Then, the proposed schemes extend to simulating curve diffusion, mean curvature flow, and surface diffusion. Finally, numerical experiments demonstrate geometric accuracy, energy decay, good mesh distribution, and high performance of the proposed schemes.

items.title: 6G Uplink Waveform and Rank Selection under Distributed Reception
items.summary: The development of 6G uplink is expanding waveform and spatial transmission options, while distributed reception makes their relative merits depend on the spatial and frequency structure of the aggregate channel. We study the joint selection of cyclic prefix orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing and discrete Fourier transform spread OFDM at rank 1 and noncoherent rank 2 under common user equipment power constraints and centralized linear minimum mean-square error reception. We derive waveform switching thresholds at both ranks and a rank selection margin, establishing conditions for selecting among the four modes based on available transmit power, DFT despreading loss, and spatial multiplexing gain. We then characterize how port gains and correlations at individual access points (APs) form aggregate spatial separation and influence mode selection. At fixed port gains and available transmit powers, improving spatial separation without reducing it on any subcarrier increases the rank selection margin, while its effect on the preferred waveform within rank 2 depends on the frequency distribution of the improvement. Numerical results show that different AP deployments can favor different waveforms and ranks, even with the same receive antenna budget and comparable aggregate channel gains, including waveform switches at a fixed preferred rank.

items.title: Smoothed analysis of stability radii for the assignment problem
items.summary: Every linear program can tolerate small changes to its costs and still yield a solution of the original problem. The size of this tolerance measures how robust an optimal decision is to noise or numerical error, and how much regularization the problem can support. Classical sensitivity analysis can determine this tolerance only from an optimal solution. This paper provides a priori lower bounds on two measures of this tolerance -- the optimality gap and the $\infty$-norm stability radius -- for the $n$-by-$n$ linear assignment problem over the Birkhoff polytope. The bounds derive from a smoothed analysis, which adds Gaussian noise with standard deviation of at least $σ$ in every direction to an arbitrary base cost. At every fixed confidence level, uniformly over the base cost, both quantities are at least of order $σ/(n\sqrt{\log n})$. The radius bound is asymptotically sharp. Under isotropic noise, the worst case occurs when every assignment has equal cost, and in this case, a scaled stability radius converges in distribution to a standard exponential variable.

items.title: Second-Order Asymptotics for the Scalar Gaussian Broadcast Channel
items.summary: This paper characterizes the second-order coding region of the scalar Gaussian broadcast channel along the curved boundary of its capacity region. The characterization holds under both average and maximal error criteria and allows correlation between the receiver noises. At each interior point of this boundary, the second-order region is a halfspace, as in the work of Scarlett and the author on Gaussian multiple-access channels with degraded message sets. Achievability follows from spherical superposition coding with a blocklength-dependent power allocation. The main innovation lies in the converse. Using Ornstein--Uhlenbeck entropy dissipation and Gaussian functional inequalities, we construct an auxiliary observation through an additive Gaussian noise channel and establish quantitative relative entropy bounds for the channel output distributions conditioned on this observation. The strong functional representation lemma of Li and El Gamal then allows us to select a realization of its independent random seed to obtain a deterministic partition of the retained receiver-1 message set. The component label plays a role analogous to the auxiliary random variable in the capacity characterization, while providing the distributional control needed at the second-order scale. These properties guide the construction of auxiliary output measures whose likelihood ratios admit the cancellations and normal approximation needed to evaluate an information spectrum converse.

items.title: A logarithm-free subexponential algorithm for minimum quartet inconsistency
items.summary: We give a deterministic algorithm for complete, unweighted minimum quartet inconsistency (MQI) with time and space $2^{O(k^{1/4})}+n^{O(1)}$, where $n$ is the number of taxa and~$k$ is the allowed number of quartet disagreements. This removes the logarithmic factor from the exponent of the MQI bound announced in 2009. The algorithm combines low-error anchoring, chromatic coding, and dynamic programming that accounts for disagreements with all input quartets, with a refined count of colorings and merging states. We also record a generic ETH-based lower bound. The optimality of the fourth-root exponent remains open.

items.title: Distributionally Robust Optimization over Incomparable Spaces
items.summary: Distributionally robust optimization (DRO) provides a principled framework for making decisions under uncertainty when the underlying distribution may be incorrectly specified. A widely used approach builds on ideas from optimal transport (OT) as a means of measuring differences between distributions. However, this depends on these distributions residing in the same space. In certain settings, the reference data distribution we have and the space on which we make our decision may be different, which renders classical OT techniques impossible. In this paper, we provide a new DRO formulation in which ambiguity sets are defined through the Gromov-Wasserstein distance, which is an extension of OT to pairs of distributions residing in incomparable spaces. We show that several seemingly unrelated optimization formulations, including conditional value-at-risk minimization, group distributionally robust optimization, robust graph $k$-median, and $k$-median with outliers, can be recovered as special cases of our formulation. We describe the computational aspects of solving the proposed formulation based on the doubly-nonnegative relaxation. Last, we illustrate the framework through experiments on clustering over incomparable spaces and stochastic graph $k$-median.

items.title: A Deterministic O(log m)-Competitive Algorithm for Online Minimum Cost Bipartite Matching with Delays
items.summary: In the online Minimum cost Bipartite Perfect Matching with Delays (MBPMD) problem, $m$ requests and $m$ servers arrive over time in a metric space. An online algorithm has to match each request to a server and can postpone a matching decision by paying the delay cost. The objective is to minimize the total distance and delay cost. Azar, Chiplunkar, and Kaplan gave a randomized $O(\log n)$-competitive algorithm for metric spaces with $n$ points that are known in advance. For deterministic algorithms, however, the best known competitive ratio in general metric spaces was $O(m^{0.59})$, due to Azar and Jacob-Fanani. On the line, Kuo proposed the Virtual Robust Matching (VRM) algorithm and showed that it is $O(\sqrt{m}\log^2 m)$-competitive. We prove that VRM is $O(\log m)$-competitive for the MBPMD problem in any metric space. VRM is deterministic and does not need to know the metric space or $m$ in advance. It is the first deterministic polylogarithmic-competitive algorithm for the MBPMD problem in general metric spaces. Unlike the previous analysis of VRM, our analysis does not rely on a geometric decomposition of the metric space. Instead, it charges the waiting time of requests over time to the edges of a fixed optimal matching. We also extend VRM to the non-bipartite version and prove that the resulting deterministic algorithm is $O(\log m)$-competitive. This improves the $O(\log^5 m)$ bound of Dufay and Wattenhofer and matches a concurrent result of Ahmadian, Chawla, Kumar, Purohit, and Zhang. The proof that VRM is $O(\log m)$-competitive and its non-bipartite extension were found by GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI) with almost no human input. We used Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic) to simplify and present the results. See the AI Usage and Methodology section for details. We take full responsibility for this paper.

items.title: Secrecy Sum-Rate Maximization for RSMA-Enabled Pinching-Antenna Systems
items.summary: This paper investigates secrecy sum-rate (SSR) maximization in a downlink rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA)-enabled single-waveguide pinching-antenna system (PASS) with an external eavesdropper. The RSMA power allocation, secure common-rate allocation, and pinching-antenna (PA) positions are jointly optimized subject to transmit-power, per-user secrecy-rate, and PA-placement constraints. To tackle the resulting nonconvex problem, an alternating-optimization framework is developed, combining successive convex approximation for RSMA resource allocation with feasibility-preserving projected gradient ascent for PA-position optimization. Numerical results show that the proposed design consistently outperforms the considered benchmarks in terms of average SSR, demonstrating the benefits of joint RSMA resource and PA-position optimization for secure PASS transmission.

items.title: Rank-Optimal Sample Complexity of Riemannian Gauss-Newton for Low-Rank Matrix Recovery
items.summary: In this paper, we study the recovery of an unknown rank-$r$ matrix $\boldsymbol{X}_\star \in \mathbb{R}^{n_1\times n_2}$ from Gaussian linear measurements using the Riemannian Gauss-Newton (RGN) algorithm. Each iteration of RGN solves the RGN equation followed by a fixed-rank retraction. We prove that, with high probability, RGN with spectral initialization converges quadratically to $\boldsymbol{X}_\star$ using $\mathcal{O} ( r(n_1+n_2)κ^2 )$ measurements, where $κ$ is the condition number of $\boldsymbol{X}_\star$. This is the first result to simultaneously achieve rank-optimal sample complexity and quadratic convergence for Gaussian low-rank matrix sensing. The key to the proof is a sharp spectral-norm analysis of the iterates, which requires controlling the inverse operator arising from the RGN equation. Our analysis develops an exact finite Neumann expansion of this inverse operator and combines it with a virtual-sequence decoupling argument and the restricted isometry property. Extensive numerical experiments support our theoretical findings and demonstrate the advantages of RGN.

items.title: Strong convergence of a slowly damped primal-dual dynamical system with general time-scaling, Tikhonov regularization and implicit Hessian damping
items.summary: This paper proposes a novel mixed-order inertial primal-dual dynamical system with general time-scaling and Tikhonov regularization coefficients, together with implicit Hessian damping, for solving convex optimization problems with linear equality constraints in Hilbert spaces. The proposed dynamical system incorporates slowly vanishing viscous damping and is developed based on a time-dependent Tikhonov-regularized Lagrangian. Under suitable assumptions, we establish fast convergence rates for the objective residual, the feasibility violation, and the primal-dual gap using a Lyapunov analysis. Moreover, we prove that the generated primal-dual trajectory converges strongly to the minimum-norm primal-dual solution. Numerical experiments illustrate the theoretical results and indicate improved convergence performance relative to the comparison dynamical systems.

items.title: Robust preconditioners for finite element approximations of control-state constrained optimal control problems governed by elliptic equations
items.summary: The goal of this paper is to derive robust preconditioners for integral control-state constrained optimal control problems governed by the second order partial differential equations with linear finite element approximations. We give corresponding discretized systems of the first order necessary and sufficient optimality conditions, and get six linear algebraic systems with saddle point schemes. Furthermore, we propose efficient block preconditioners to solve the corresponding linearized algebraic systems. With respect to both mesh sizes and inherent parameters, the robustness of proposed preconditioners is proved with explicit eigenvalues of minimal polynomials. Meanwhile, we design two algorithms and choose the incomplete $LU$ factorizations to deduce the computations. Two numerical experiments are given to depict the efficiency of our proposed preconditioners.

items.title: Variance Reduction Note 3: The Convergence of PAGE
items.summary: The probabilistic gradient estimator (PAGE) alternates randomly between an accurate gradient refresh and a cheap recursive correction. This third expository note on recursive variance reduction explains the algorithm and gives a self-contained convergence proof for smooth nonconvex optimization. A Lyapunov function combines objective decrease with estimation error, turning the refresh probability into an explicit contraction parameter. The resulting expected oracle complexity is $O(n+\sqrt n\,ε^{-2})$ for finite sums and $O(ε^{-3})$ for online problems, with the other problem parameters fixed. Initialization, refreshes, and both evaluations in each gradient difference are counted. The presentation is pedagogical and makes no claim of a new algorithm or convergence rate.

items.title: Robust Appointment Scheduling with Heterogeneous Costs
items.summary: Designing simple appointment systems that under uncertainty in service times, try to achieve both high utilization of expensive medical equipment and personnel as well as short waiting time for patients, has long been an interesting and challenging problem in health care. We consider a robust version of the appointment scheduling problem, introduced by Mittal et al.\ (2014), with the goal of finding simple and easy-to-use algorithms. Previous work focused on the special case where per-unit costs due to under-utilization of equipment/personnel are homogeneous i.e., costs are linear and identical. We consider the heterogeneous case and devise an LP that has a simple closed-form solution. This solution yields the first constant-factor approximation for the problem. We also find special cases beyond homogeneous costs where the LP leads to closed form optimal schedules. Our approach and results extend more generally to convex piece-wise linear costs. For the case where the order of patients is changeable, we focus on linear costs and show that the problem is strongly NP-hard when the under-utilization costs are heterogeneous. For changeable order with homogeneous under-utilization costs, it was previously shown that an EPTAS exists. We instead find an extremely simple, ratio-based ordering that is 1.0604 approximate.

items.title: Fully Discrete Error Analysis of the CSLDG Scheme with Numerical Characteristic Tracing and Spline Reconstruction
items.summary: A semi-Lagrangian discontinuous finite element scheme based on the characteristic Galerkin method (CSLDG) is investigated.The scheme directly discretizes an integral invariant model derived from the coupling of the transport equation and its adjoint equation.we have established, for the first time, error estimates for the fully discrete CSLDG scheme over a general domain Ωin \mathbb{R}^d.The error is decomposed into three parts: the ideal numerical solution error (the difference between the exact solution and the spatial discretization), the time-dependent test function error (the deviation of the test function caused by the numerical characteristic backtracking via an ODE solver), and the upstream region approximation error (the integration region deviation induced by numerical characteristic backtracking and spline boundary reconstruction).Under either compact-support boundary conditions or periodic boundary conditions with the velocity field and the solution sharing the same spatial periodicity, without requiring incompressibility,and assuming the standard CFL condition (Δt=O(h)) linking the time step and the mesh size, the following results are proved:Using piecewise P^K polynomial spaces, the L^2 error of the ideal numerical solution attains a suboptimal order O(h^K); If the ODE solver order satisfies D \ge 2K+2+d, the overall error retains the suboptimal order even after incorporating the time-dependent test function error;When the upstream region approximation error is further taken into account, for d \ge 2 the overall error remains suboptimal O(h^K) provided the spline reconstruction degree satisfies r \ge \max(K+1+d, d+2);

items.title: Variational learning of energy-stable macroscopic flow equations from microscopic laws
items.summary: We present a generalized variational approach for constructing energy-stable macroscopic partial differential equations (PDEs) directly from microscopic physical laws. Rather than fitting the PDE evolution for prescribed variables from macroscopic trajectories, we construct an extendable variational structure by adjoining auxiliary variables to seek autonomous reduced dynamics in an enlarged state space. By defining these variables as micro--macro encoders with explicit microscopic counterparts, we cast the learning problem as the sample-wise joint identification of the reduced state representation and the variational ingredients from time-discrete data, enabling systematic law-level transfer across scales. The resulting PDEs preserve frame indifference, physical constraints, and energy stability by construction, and admit a fluctuation--dissipation-consistent stochastic extension. Numerical results for the non-Newtonian hydrodynamics of polymeric fluids show that the learned models capture the viscoelastic responses induced by nonlinear and heterogeneous molecular interactions beyond empirical closures.

items.title: Longest-Queue Policies in Dynamic Matching with Abandonments
items.summary: We study a dynamic two-way matching market in which agents of heterogeneous types arrive over time, wait to be matched according to a compatibility network, and abandon the system if their random patience expires. The decision maker collects match rewards and pays holding and abandonment costs, and seeks to maximize the expected net value over a finite horizon. We evaluate policies by their approximation ratio against a fluid benchmark, the optimal value of a linear-programming relaxation that upper bounds the expected net value of every policy. Under a general position gap (GPG) condition, which requires the unique optimal dual solution of this linear program to remain optimal under small perturbations of the arrival rates, we propose a longest-queue policy. The policy first uses this dual solution to identify a set of good match types and a set of critical agent types. Upon each arrival, it considers only good matches and matches the arrival to the critical partner with the longest queue subject to availabilities. In the high-volume regime, in which arrival rates are scaled by s, we prove that the policy attains an approximation ratio of at least 1-O(1/s) at every scale s >= 1 and every horizon T >= 1, so the ratio tends to 1 as s goes to infinity.

items.title: Extensible Programmatic Specification of Finite Element Methods
items.summary: Finite element methods (FEMs) are a powerful and ubiquitous tool for solving engineering problems. Experimenting with different finite elements can improve the quality and efficiency of solutions. In some cases, the wrong (but nonetheless most common) choice of finite element will produce solutions which converge to the wrong answer regardless of mesh resolution. However, in practice, the choice of finite element is not explored due to the complexity of re-deriving and re-implementing finite element methods. Trying a new finite element is challenging because practitioners must manually deduce formulas to use these elements and implement them within a potentially complex system. We address this problem by introducing ElementForge, a finite element system that is parametric over the literate mathematical specification of a finite element in a domain-specific language (DSL). The ElementForge compiler reasons about tensor spaces, tensors, and tensor bases from first principles to derive implementations of finite elements. The ElementForge compiler is able to automatically derive implementations of finite elements previously only derived by hand. Further, ElementForge minimally couples several key mathematical concepts, mainly tensor fields, mesh topologies, sparse tensors, and assembled finite element operators, to produce a complete finite element system that is parametric over the choice of element. Consequently, the elements derived by the compiler can be applied parametrically to new meshes, PDEs, and boundary conditions. We evaluate our system by implementing several simulations with different finite elements, demonstrating that our system can explore tradeoffs in generality, accuracy, speed, and representational complexity. For example, we are able to implement the Morley, Bell, Argyris, and Hermite like elements with less than 50 lines of code and use them all in a single simulation.

items.title: Deterministic $n^{O(\log n)}$ Graph Isomorphism Algorithm via Inherited Decompositions
items.summary: We give a deterministic $n^{O(\log n)}$-time algorithm for graph isomorphism. To our knowledge, this is the first proof of such a worst-case bound for general graphs. The algorithm uses the local-certificate and color-refinement steps of Babai's quasipolynomial algorithm, but retains the decomposition of each recursive instance when it solves an auxiliary coloring problem. There are two reasons for retaining this information. First, a local test can make progress without removing many vertices: it can eliminate a layer of permutation symmetry. A logarithmic bound on the total weight of these layers allows tests of constant size. Second, the auxiliary bipartite graphs arising in the symmetry-breaking step can be represented inside the current instance, after retaining a row decomposition when necessary. These recursive calls inherit the progress already made. The analysis gives a recurrence with quadratic logarithmic cost and a fixed power decrease in every fresh recursive call, improving the explicit cubic logarithmic exponent in the analysis of the corrected Luks--Babai algorithm. We present the algorithm through colorings, partitions, and bipartite graphs, and collect the permutation-group ingredients in one appendix. The result extends to string isomorphism and returns one isomorphism and generators for the full automorphism group.

items.title: Three-phase time minimization transportation problem with non-idle phases: a polynomial two-witness algorithm
items.summary: The three-phase time minimization transportation problem partitions the origin-terminal links into three sets used in consecutive phases and minimizes the sum of the phase shipment times. Optimal solutions may leave a phase idle, as in the main example of the original study. We require every phase to carry a positive integer quantity while leaving the split of the total requirement across phases free. Discarding idle solutions from the original algorithm does not, in general, solve this variant. We prove that the optimum is attained by fixing one witness link in each of two phases and deciding the third phase by a single network flow computation, with the optimal Phase-3 time of each witness pair located by binary search. The resulting exact algorithm is strongly polynomial. It extends to any fixed number of phases, whereas, when the number of phases is part of the input, even non-idle feasibility is strongly NP-complete; feasibility alone is fixed-parameter tractable in the number of phases via known rainbow-matching results. We also characterize the minimum time of each phase. On the main example, non-idleness raises the optimum from 38 to 41. On 3,650 random instances with up to $50\times50$ links the algorithm took at most 50.2 seconds, and non-idleness raised the optimal value in 41% of the 2,250 instances with equal phase sizes; on 90 sampled instances it was faster than a mixed integer programming solver on 80 with a direct formulation and on 65 with a tighter threshold formulation.

items.title: Differentially Private Distributed Optimization via the Intrinsic Randomness of Zeroth-Order Estimators: Sampling Geometry, Convergence, and Privacy Guarantees
items.summary: Distributed zeroth-order optimization has gained increasing attention in applications where exact gradients are computationally expensive or unavailable. However, the iterative exchange of local decision variables makes distributed networks vulnerable to inference attacks. While differential privacy provides a rigorous framework for privacy protection, conventional approaches generally require additional random noise, which inevitably affects optimization accuracy. In this paper, we investigate whether the randomness inherent in zeroth-order estimation can itself provide privacy protection. We develop a distributed zeroth-order gradient descent method that integrates consensus updates with a ball-uniform two-point gradient estimator. Our theoretical analysis shows that our algorithm attains standard convergence guarantees in both online and offline optimization settings. We then characterize the relevant probability distributions of the associated privacy mechanism, and establish differential privacy guarantees for both the online and offline optimization settings. These results reveal the potential of intrinsic zeroth-order randomness for privacy protection.

items.title: An $\mathsf{FPRAS}$ for Mixed Volumes
items.summary: We design the first fully polynomial-time randomized approximation scheme ($\mathsf{FPRAS}$) to estimate the mixed volume of $n$ arbitrary compact convex sets in $\mathbb{R}^{n}$ specified by weak membership oracles. This disproves a longstanding conjecture of Gurvits (2009). $\textbf{AI Disclosure}$ The main ideas were generated entirely by GPT 6 Astra. The purpose of this paper is to provide a human-written exposition of the algorithm.

items.title: Bilinear Hulls for Support Splitting: Characterization, Optimization, and Applications
items.summary: Sendrier's Support Splitting Algorithm (SSA) is the standard solver for the Permutation Equivalence Problem (PEP); its cost is dominated by a term that grows exponentially in the hull dimension. We study, mathematically, how much this cost can be lowered by replacing the standard inner product, on which the hull is defined, with an alternative bilinear form. Two structural results give a complete answer: only a narrow two-parameter family of bilinear forms produces a hull on which SSA can still operate, namely those whose matrix in the standard basis is a linear combination of the identity and the all-ones matrix; and even within this family the hull dimension drops by at most one (with the reduction achieved on every self-dual code whose length is coprime to the field characteristic). Together, these results give a tight upper bound: since SSA on a code with hull dimension $h$ has cost dominated by $q^h$, replacing the standard hull with $\mathrm{Hull}_M$ lowers this dominant term from $q^h$ to at best $q^{h-1}$, so no bilinear-form generalization of the inner product can reduce the SSA cost by more than a factor of $q$, the field size. Going beyond this requires invariants outside the bilinear framework. As an application, we verify that PEP-based SPECK admits the factor-$q$ cost reduction, while LEP-based LESS and PKP-based PERK lie outside our framework. A SageMath implementation of the bilinear-hull preprocessing confirms feasibility at SPECK's recommended length $n = 252$.

items.title: A Decomposition Theorem and a Simple Algorithm for Contraction Fixed Points
items.summary: We prove a decomposition theorem for the problem of computing an approximate fixed point of a contraction map $f\colon [0,1]^k \to [0,1]^k$ under the $\ell_{\infty}$-norm. After a preliminary version of the decomposition theorem appeared on arXiv [CLY26], Feodorov and Haslebacher [FH26] gave a striking application of the theorem, showing that it can be used to convert any $\operatorname{poly}(k,\log(1/\varepsilon))$-query algorithm with running time $(k\log(1/\varepsilon))^{O(k)}$ into an algorithm with running time $(k\log(1/\varepsilon))^{O(\sqrt{k})}$. They instantiated this framework with an $O(k^2\log(1/\varepsilon))$-query algorithm with the desired running time, thereby obtaining the first subexponential-time algorithm for contraction fixed points under the $\ell_{\infty}$-norm and, via well-known reductions, the first deterministic subexponential-time algorithm for simple stochastic games and mean-payoff games. In addition to the decomposition theorem, as our second main result in this paper, we show that the $O(k\log(1/\varepsilon))$-query algorithm of [CLY25] can be implemented in time $(k\log(1/\varepsilon))^{O(k)}$; our algorithm may be viewed as conceptually simpler compared to the algorithm of [FH26]. A key observation here is that the function constructed in [CLY25], whose fixed points are used as the next query points, turns out to be nonexpansive under the $\ell_{\infty}$-norm, so the brute-force procedure can be replaced by known algorithms for contraction fixed points.

items.title: Accelerating posterior sampling in Bayesian inverse problems with diffusion models: an online-offline perspective
items.summary: Bayesian inverse problems require both informative prior models and computationally feasible posterior inference. Score-based diffusion models provide expressive learned priors, but their use for inversion introduces a conditioning problem: the score of a noised posterior is generally unavailable from a prior score alone. This selective survey reviews the principal approaches to that problem, including likelihood guidance, spectral and projection methods, sequential Monte Carlo corrections, and amortized conditional training. We organize methods by how they split cost between offline preparation and online inference, and compare their assumptions, advantages and limitations, with emphasis on computational speedups. Some ongoing directions and open questions are gathered at the end.

items.title: Reading between the levels: new tools for the Thorup-Zwick hierarchy and their applications
items.summary: In this paper, we develop three new analytical tools for the Thorup-Zwick hierarchy: the Mixed-Level Growth, Two-Level Growth, and Long-Short Growth lemmas. Using these tools, we obtain improved approximate distance oracles (ADOs), and algorithms for $n$-pairs shortest paths ($n$-PSP), multiple-source shortest paths (MSSP), and $ST$-shortest paths, as well as new hopsets. One of our main results is a $(\frac 65 k+O(1))$-stretch ADO with $\tilde O(mn^{1/k})$ preprocessing time and space (where $\tilde O$ hides polylogarithmic factors), and $\tilde O(n^{1/k})$ query time, breaking, for sparse graphs, the $(2k-O(1))$-stretch barrier for ADOs with $\tilde O(n^{1+1/k})$ space and $\tilde O(n^{1/k})$ query time. In unweighted graphs, we also obtain a $(\frac 65 k+O(1),O(k))$-approximate ADO with $\tilde O(n^{1+1/k})$ space and $\tilde O(n^{1/k})$ query time. This also yields a $(\frac 65 k+O(1))$-approximation algorithm for $m$-pairs shortest paths ($m$-PSP) in $\tilde O(mn^{1/k})$ time, answering the question of Chechik, Hoch, and Lifshitz [SODA'25] of whether the $2k-O(1)$ barrier for $n$-PSP in $\tilde O(mn^{1/k})$ time can be broken. For unweighted graphs, we give a new analysis of the existing $\tilde O(mn^{1/k}+n^{1+2/k})$-time $n$-PSP algorithm of [Chechik et al., SODA'25], and show that, without any modification, it is a $(k,k-1)$-approximation, i.e., $d(u,v)\le\hat d(u,v)\le k\cdot d(u,v)+k-1$ for every queried pair. This improves its multiplicative factor from $\frac 43 k+O(1)$ to $k$, and the leading coefficient $k$ is tight for this algorithm. Moreover, for graphs with $m=Ω(n^{1+1/k})$, this answers the question of Dalirrooyfard et al. [FOCS'22] up to the additive $k-1$.

items.title: Likelihood-Free Schrödinger--Föllmer Sampling for Bayesian Inference with Fixed-Proposal Reuse
items.summary: We study Bayesian posterior sampling when the likelihood is an expectation that is costly to evaluate. We construct a likelihood-free Schrödinger--Föllmer sampler whose drift is written as a ratio of expectations over Gaussian variables and simulator outputs and is estimated directly from joint draws of the two. Importance sampling with a fixed proposal allows the simulator outputs to be generated once and reused across all time steps and trajectories. For the likelihood-free Schrödinger--Föllmer sampler, which draws new Monte Carlo samples at each step, we bound the terminal Wasserstein error under regularity and moment assumptions, separating time-discretization and integration errors. For the likelihood-free Schrödinger--Föllmer sampler with sample reuse, we prove that the output converges to the posterior in the Wasserstein distance, assuming only a finite posterior second moment. Numerical experiments illustrate the reduction in simulator calls and the benefits of randomized quasi-Monte Carlo for drift estimation.

items.title: Mixed-Integer Programming for Causal Discovery with Unknown Hard-Intervention Targets
items.summary: When intervention targets are uncertain, learning causal relationships and identifying directly perturbed variables become a joint task. We develop an exact mixed-integer program based on optimized parent-set scores (PS-MIP) for joint graph and intervention-target estimation in linear Gaussian structural equation models under stochastic hard interventions. The method can incorporate candidate-edge restrictions and partial target knowledge when available. For each random variable, PS-MIP evaluates candidate sets of direct causes, or parent sets, by optimizing the likelihood parameters and compatible target patterns, retaining both the score and a minimizing target pattern. A global mixed-integer program then selects parent sets subject to acyclicity. Under stated conditions, this reduction preserves the joint objective and reconstructs the graph, targets, and likelihood parameters. Because the local scores are precomputed, PS-MIP replaces a direct large bilinear mixed-integer program with a linear selection problem; empirically it certifies global optimality on far more instances than the direct formulation (126 of 180 versus 34) and is often orders of magnitude faster. On synthetic data, PS-MIP achieves favorable false-discovery--true-discovery trade-offs relative to several benchmark algorithms for causal discovery with unknown intervention targets, along with strong intervention-target recovery in denser settings. An exploratory study on real data from a controlled physical system further demonstrates recovery beyond simulation.

items.title: Singular Perturbations for Control Systems Safety
items.summary: Control Barrier Functions (CBFs) offer a powerful theory for enforcing safety in dynamical systems. Yet, applying this framework to complex systems is challenging when subsystems are feedback-interconnected and operate at different timescales. Such structures arise naturally in multiphysics systems and in control architectures where physical plants interact with optimization, estimation, and control algorithms. In many of these settings, safety involves only part of the system, motivating the design of reduced-order certificates. Inspired by singular perturbation theory, we establish sufficient conditions, involving separation between slow and fast dynamics, under which a reduced-order safety certificate can be lifted to the full interconnected system. Specifically, we construct a composite CBF ensuring forward invariance of a lifted subset of the original safe set. We also show that the certified safe set expands monotonically as the tuning parameter accelerating the fast dynamics is reduced. Numerical results validate the approach on two robotic systems: a planar 2-DoF manipulator with motor dynamics and a 6-DoF UR10e manipulator controlled by a suboptimal optimization algorithm.

items.title: A Numerical Refinement of an Exact Discrete Fourier Transform Bound
items.summary: We refine the numerical bounds in Kartal's instantiation of Sussman's exact discrete Fourier transform construction. For every integer n >= 1, the resulting algorithm computes the length-n transform with work O(n (log n)^(1 - delta)), where delta = 0.0030201659. The bound holds in an exact complex-arithmetic RAM model with a supplied canonical root of unity. This final exponent saving exceeds the earlier certified parameter C_0 = 0.00302016 by 5.9 x 10^(-9). We retain the underlying circuit, tighten rational bounds for sums of powers of its block and target ranks, and increase the fixed tensor power from 7760 to 11640. These bounds establish the inequalities for Sussman's recursion at the intermediate certificate parameter C = 0.00302016595. The gap C - delta absorbs the overhead of recursion and Fourier reduction. The resulting transform theorem is proved in Lean and checked against the reference problem statement.

items.title: Model-Based Co-Clustering for Censored Data
items.summary: Co-clustering jointly partitions the rows and columns of a data matrix. Standard co-clustering methods for continuous data typically assume that entries are observed exactly. Matrices with censored entries, such as assay measurements below a detection limit, are therefore commonly completed by substitution or imputation before co-clustering. Since the completed values are treated as exact, the estimated block means and partitions depend on the completion rule. We propose the censored Gaussian latent block model (CGLBM), in which each censored entry contributes the probability of its reported interval. We establish identifiability under a known Type I censoring design. Approximate standard errors for the block means follow from the Fisher information under censoring. CGLBM is fitted by a generalized expectation--maximization algorithm, and its row and column class numbers are selected by a BIC approximation to the integrated classification likelihood. In simulation studies, boundary substitution and truncated normal imputation attenuate the contrasts between block means, whereas the partition recovery of multiple imputation drops the most under heavy censoring. CGLBM preserves the contrasts, and its partition recovery drops the least. The method is implemented in the R package CGLBM.

items.title: Entropic Column Generation and Lehmer Branch-and-Price for Bin Packing Problem
items.summary: We introduce Lehmer branch-and-price, an exact algorithm for bin packing and cutting stock problems built on the Lehmer transform, the ratio of Mellin transforms of item weights at consecutive orders. The transform maps each bin, a finite multiset of item weights, to a smooth increasing curve, and so gives the discrete problem a continuous representation on which the tools of analysis, such as convexity, exponential families and smoothing, can act. Read along this curve, the problem yields an explicit dual solution, a monotone representation of the dominance order, a family of constructive heuristics with first fit decreasing as its limit, and an integer identity that tells when the linear relaxation can decide an instance and when only a perfect packing can improve the best solution known. Lifted from items to patterns, the transform gives entropic column generation, a new form of column generation that bounds the relaxation from both sides at every iteration without solving the pricing problem exactly, maximizes a smoothed dual at an explicit rate, and measures by an entropy how much the relaxation leaves undecided. We show that the proposed algorithm outperforms the state-of-the-art methods on the standard benchmark in both the number of instances solved and the computational time.

items.title: How Much Can Approximate Equilibria Change the Social Cost of Selfish Routing?
items.summary: We study approximate Nash equilibria in nonatomic congestion games, with the goal of understanding how much the social cost can change when the equilibrium condition is relaxed. We consider $ε$-approximate Nash equilibria ($ε$-NE), in which each player uses a strategy whose cost is at most $1 + ε$ times the minimum available cost. We compare the social costs of $ε$-NE and exact Nash equilibria. This lets us quantify, for example, how much a navigation app can reduce total travel time when drivers tolerate routes slightly slower than the fastest available route. For degree-$d$ polynomial latencies in both general nonatomic congestion games and single-commodity routing games on series-parallel networks, we give tight lower and upper bounds on the relative change in social cost from an exact Nash equilibrium to any $ε$-NE, with matching instances for every $ε$. For small $ε$, the largest possible relative reduction and increase in general congestion games are both $Θ(\sqrt{dε})$, independently of the number of resources and populations. In contrast, on series-parallel networks of depth $h$, the largest possible relative reduction is $Θ(hε)$, while the largest possible relative increase is known to be $ε$. For the classes of games we study, these results give a tight and quantitative characterization of the possible changes in social cost and establish a separation between general and series-parallel networks.

items.title: Online Autotuning of Algebraic Multigrid via Contextual Bandits and Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: Algebraic multigrid (AMG) methods are widely used for solving large sparse linear systems, but their efficiency depends strongly on interacting setup and solve parameters. Effective parameter choices typically depend on the problem. We develop a phase-aware online autotuning method for hypre's BoomerAMG to reduce cumulative time-to-solution over sequences of related linear systems. A LinUCB-based contextual bandit selects mixed-type parameters for AMG hierarchy construction using a shared cost model over PDE descriptors and configuration encodings. A recursive LSTDQ controller uses residual and timing observations to estimate the AMG solve time within each attempt and adapt relaxation weights between multigrid cycles. Both learners update from ongoing solves without offline pretraining. Across grids of sizes $40^3$, $60^3$, and $80^3$, the joint autotuning method reduces total runtime, including recurring learner computation, by 36.1-43.3% for diffusion problems and 19.8-31.0% for diffusion-advection problems over sequences of 5000 linear systems, relative to the reference BoomerAMG default configuration. On a variable-flow diffusion-advection benchmark comprising 30,000 systems on a $60^3$ grid, 2 systems fail to converge with joint autotuning, compared with 1677 for the reference configuration, under their respective attempt budgets.

items.title: Fluid Limits and Upper Bounds for Randomized Greedy Matching
items.summary: The Modified Randomized Greedy (MRG) algorithm [Tinhofer (1984), Aronson-Dyer-Frieze-Suen (1995)] is a classical greedy algorithm for finding approximate maximum matchings. MRG repeatedly picks a uniformly random unmatched vertex and matches it to a uniformly random unmatched neighbor, if one exists. Since 1991, the best upper bound on its approximation ratio has been $2/3$, given by the Bomb graphs of [Dyer and Frieze (1991)]. We improve this bound to $0.6569$ on general graphs and $0.6607$ on bipartite graphs. Our constructions consist of copies of small gadgets, with specified vertex classes joined completely. We track each algorithm by counting gadget copies with each possible configuration of remaining vertices. Wormald's differential equation method [Wormald (1995)] shows that these counts, scaled by the size parameter of the construction, converge to a deterministic trajectory known as the \textit{fluid limit}, which is described by ordinary differential equations. This fluid limit approximation holds while the relevant vertex classes have positive density, and so we devise a separate counting argument determines the contribution from the end of the run. Furthermore, we apply our framework to Random Decision Order (RDO), in which vertices are processed in uniformly random order and choose unmatched neighbors according to fixed adversarial preferences. On bipartite graphs, we determine the exact limiting ratio on the Double-Bomb family of [Tang-Wu-Zhang (2020)]. Its minimum is $31/48$, confirming their numerical estimate of about $0.646$.On general graphs, we improve their upper bound of $5/8$, given by the paw graph, to $0.5946$ on a new family. Finally, we give one possible explanation for why $2/3$ seemed to be optimal for MRG in the concluding remarks.

items.title: An Incidence-Based Edge-Averaged Method for Convection-Diffusion Problems on Polytopal Meshes
items.summary: We develop an incidence-based edge-averaged method for scalar convection-diffusion problems on convex polytopal meshes in arbitrary dimensions. The proposed method extends the classical edge-averaged finite-element scheme through a graph-theoretic formulation based on vertex-edge incidence matrices. We first establish this formulation on simplices in arbitrary dimensions and then extend it to convex polytopes by introducing complementary edges and generalized barycentric coordinates. A key ingredient is a matrix identity that relates the generalized Whitney edge mass matrix to a diagonal representation of the Poisson stiffness matrix, enabling an exponentially-fitted discretization expressed entirely in terms of nodal values and edge weights. We prove that the resulting stiffness matrix is a nonsingular $M$-matrix under suitable positivity and connectivity conditions, ensuring monotonicity and the discrete maximum principle. Numerical experiments on two- and three-dimensional simplicial and nonsimplicial meshes demonstrate first-order convergence in the $H^1$ semi-norm and stable, nonoscillatory solutions in convection-dominated regimes.

items.title: The Movement Complexity of Sorting
items.summary: The complexity of sorting is usually measured by the number of comparisons. This measure ignores the movement of the read heads between comparisons, which is a real cost on many machines. We study this cost on its own. Keys lie on a $d$-dimensional grid, two heads move over the grid and compare the keys beneath them, and the only cost is the total movement of the heads. The algorithm plans its route in $r$ rounds and sees the outcomes of each round only after running it. For every $d$ and $r$ we determine the expected movement needed to sort $n$ keys: it is $n^β$ up to polylogarithmic factors, where $β=1+D^{r-1}/(D^{r}-(D-1)^{r})$ and $D=2d$, falling from $n^{2}$ at $r=1$ to $n^{1+1/(2d)}$ with unlimited rounds. Our algorithm makes every round move about the same amount, and a matching lower bound holds against every algorithm.

items.title: Lower Bounds on Inference Complexity for Polyak-Ruppert Averaged Stochastic Gradient Descent
items.summary: In this paper, we establish sharp lower bounds for Gaussian approximation of Polyak-Ruppert averaged stochastic gradient descent with polynomially decreasing step sizes. For every fixed exponent $γ\in(1/2,1)$, a single one-dimensional smooth, strongly convex example has approximation error with the limiting variance of order $n^{1/2-γ}+n^{γ-1}$ in Kolmogorov and convex distances. This matches the existing upper bound throughout the range of $γ$. The nonlinear bias contributes $n^{1/2-γ}$ even when the Gaussian reference uses the finite linearized variance. We also derive a lower bound of order $n^{-(1-γ)/2}$ for the relative mean error of estimating the limiting variance from one SGD trajectory, uniformly over a scalar quadratic family. With the limiting variance known, achieving approximation error $\varepsilon$ on this example takes order $\varepsilon^{-4}$ iterations for the best choice $γ=3/4$. Achieving both Gaussian approximation and relative mean variance-estimation errors at most $\varepsilon$ uniformly over the model class requires at least order $\varepsilon^{-6}$ iterations for every fixed $γ$.

items.title: Minimum-Norm Interpolation in Weighted Variation Spaces: Direct and Inverse Problems
items.summary: We study minimum-norm interpolation in weighted variation spaces generated by ReLU$^s$ ridge functions on the unit ball, where $s$ is a positive integer. For a target $f$ in the weighted variation space and a node set with sufficiently small fill distance $h$, every minimum-norm interpolant satisfies the direct bound $\|f-\mathscr{I}_{X_h}f\|_{L_2(\mathbb{B}^d)}\lesssim_{d,s}h^{(2s+1)/4}\|f\|_{\mathcal{V}_s}$. Under a boundary separation condition on the nodes, we construct a matching lower bound for the worst-case interpolation error. For the inverse problem, we introduce dual certificates and derive an estimate analogous to a Bernstein inequality. Under suitable upper bounds on dictionary size and spectral lower bounds for the atomic Gram matrices, sufficiently fast $L_2$ convergence of minimum-norm interpolants along geometrically decreasing fill distances implies that the target belongs to $\mathcal{V}_s$. As a byproduct, the best $L_2$ approximation error $E_n(f)_{L_2(\mathbb{B}^d)}$ for shallow ReLU$^s$ networks of width at most $n$ satisfies $E_n(f)_{L_2(\mathbb{B}^d)}\lesssim_{d,s}n^{-1/2-(2s+1)/(2d)}\|f\|_{\mathcal{V}_s}$, with the weighted atomic cost of an approximating network bounded by a constant multiple of $\|f\|_{\mathcal{V}_s}$, independently of $n$.

items.title: CuPH: Parallel Cubical Persistent Homology via Level-Synchronous Component Tracking
items.summary: Persistent homology (PH) is a mathematically principled multi-scale topological descriptor of shape and connectivity in data. It is widely applied in image classification, segmentation, and shape analysis across medical and aerial imaging, providing structural information that pixel-wise deep learning may overlook.
